item.title: REPLY TO OBJECTION WAS INADEQUATE (EOAK 8534/2025)
item.description:
A relative made an objection about the care of their late mother. The wellbeing services county only replied that the matter had been dealt with, because the information is confidential. According to the Ombudsman, this reply was not enough. The reply must give reasons, and it is usually possible at least to say how the matter was looked into and what was done as a result. — Opinion: the wellbeing services county acted wrongly.

source

item.title: START-UP ENTREPRENEUR PERMITS (HE 216/2026 vp)
item.description:
The Government proposes that start-up entrepreneurs should no longer apply for a separate free statement from Business Finland. The assessment would be made as part of the fee-based residence permit application. A person planning to become an entrepreneur could apply for a business ID only after receiving a residence permit. This is a proposal intended to take effect on 12 January 2028.

source

item.title: COMPULSORY EDUCATION ACT CHANGES (HE 213/2026 vp)
item.description:
In some situations a young person could complete compulsory education in a youth workshop. In the joint application for upper secondary education, applicants of compulsory school age would be admitted first. This is a proposal that would take effect at the start of 2027.

source

item.title: TAX RULES ON RESTRUCTURING (HE 211/2026 vp)
item.description:
Mergers, divisions and other business restructuring would be easier to carry out without immediate tax consequences. The right to deduct losses in such arrangements would also be extended. This is a proposal; the changes would take effect on 1 January 2027.

source

item.title: TAX EXEMPTION FOR ELTIF FUNDS (VM/2026/177)
item.description:
It would be easier to set up ELTIF funds for long-term investment in Finland, as not all investors would need to be professional investors. The conditions for tax exemption of foreign funds would be changed to match rulings of the Court of Justice of the EU. This is a proposal that would take effect at the start of 2027.

source

item.title: EHDS IMPLEMENTATION BILLS (EHDS-esitykset 1.10.2026)
item.description:
New EU rules on health data are being brought into Finnish law. People could manage their own health data better, and the data could be used more easily, for example in research. Kanta Services' personal health data repository would be closed. These are proposals that Parliament will consider.

source

item.title: MARKET SURVEILLANCE OF MACHINERY (HE 220/2026 vp)
item.description:
Market surveillance of machinery and equipment used at work would move entirely to one authority, the occupational safety and health division of the Licensing and Supervisory Authority. The EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, and breaching it could lead to a fine or a penalty. This is a proposal.

source

item.title: BASIC BANKING FOR SMALL FIRMS (VM/2026/179)
item.description:
Small businesses, associations and foundations would get a right to a bank account and other basic banking services, as private individuals already have. Banks would have to reply to customers within five banking days. This is a proposal; the acts would take effect on 1 July 2027.

source

item.title: FOREST REGENERATION NOTICE (HE 214/2026 vp)
item.description:
Forest owners would have to notify the Forest Centre once work to establish new forest after felling has been done. The notification would be free, but failing to make it would be a forest offence. This is a proposal; the changes would take effect on 1 May 2027.

source

item.title: SEVESO III: FINLAND TAKEN TO COURT (INF/26/1760)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The European Commission is taking Finland to the EU Court of Justice. According to the Commission, Finnish law does not match EU rules that aim to prevent major accidents involving dangerous substances. The problems concern inspections and people's right to information and to appeal. The Commission also wants Finland to fully implement a directive on banks. Finland has two months to reply.

source

item.title: CARTEL CASE TAKEN OVER BY EC (C-855/24 P)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The Crown companies appealed against a ruling on the European Commission's proceedings in a cartel case. The Commission had opened proceedings in a case already being handled by a national competition authority, at that authority's request. The judgment concerns, among other things, subsidiarity, good administration and a reasonable time. The outcome must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: TENANT LEGAL COSTS CLAUSE, CJEU (C-459/25)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The judgment concerns a term in a consumer lease under which the tenant pays all legal costs if the tenant fails to meet contractual obligations. The question is what follows when such a term is found to be unfair. The outcome must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: TEMPORARY PROTECTION AND ASYLUM (C-249/25)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The judgment concerns an application for international protection by a person enjoying temporary protection. The question concerns a national practice of suspending the time limit for deciding the application during the temporary protection period. The outcome must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: BETTING STAKES DEDUCTIBLE (KHO:2026:79)
item.description:
A person placed bets extensively and systematically on betting sites outside the EEA. According to the Supreme Administrative Court the betting was an income-generating activity, so the person could deduct from earned income the stakes of lost bets as well. The taxation will be partly reconsidered. — Leave to appeal was granted. The decisions of the Administrative Court and the Assessment Adjustment Board and the tax reassessment were set aside, and the matter was referred back to the Board. The Tax Administration was ordered to pay legal costs of 5 820 euros.

source

item.title: EU ACTION ON IN-GAME CURRENCIES (KKV tiedote 1.10.2026)
item.description:
Consumer authorities in EU countries are investigating whether nine popular video games follow consumer protection rules, for example in how they show prices of in-game currencies. Finland's Consumer Ombudsman is taking part. The investigations are ongoing.

source

item.title: PRIVATE EQUITY COMPANY TAXATION (KHO:2026:78)
item.description:
A private equity fund bought a group of companies through two companies set up for that purpose. According to the Supreme Administrative Court, the lower company is treated for tax purposes as a company engaged in private equity activity. This is an advance ruling for tax years 2024 and 2025. — The appeal was allowed. The decisions of the Administrative Court and the Tax Administration were set aside. Advance ruling for tax years 2024 and 2025; the matter was referred back to the Tax Administration on the second question.

source

item.title: RULE OF LAW: SEMMELWEIS UNIVERSITY (T-138/23)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
Hungary's Semmelweis University challenged the EU Council decision that barred the Commission from entering into commitments with Hungarian public interest trusts and the entities they maintain because of rule-of-law problems. The judgment concerns, among other things, the duty to state reasons and the right to be heard. The outcome must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: ENFORCING THE METHANE REGULATION (TEM tiedote 30.9.2026)
item.description:
The ministry is asking for views on a bill under which Tukes would start enforcing EU rules on methane emissions in the energy sector. A company breaking the rules could face, for example, a fine or a warning. Comments may be submitted until 21.10.2026.

source

item.title: GYM NOTICE PERIOD TO MARKET COURT (KKV tiedote 30.9.2026)
item.description:
According to the Consumer Ombudsman, the gym chain Fitness24Seven ties customers for too long, as the notice period for membership is two months. The Ombudsman asks the Market Court to prohibit the term. The case is pending, and the Market Court will decide it.

source

item.title: DVV NOT LIABLE FOR APPEAL COSTS (KKO:2026:73)
item.description:
The Digital and Population Data Services Agency asked a court to replace an adult's mother with a public guardian as the adult's guardian. The Court of Appeal overturned the District Court's decision granting the application and ordered the agency to pay the other side's costs. According to the Supreme Court there was no special reason for this, so the agency does not pay the costs. — DVV was not ordered to pay A's and B's legal costs in the Court of Appeal.

source

item.title: RECOVERY OF SOCIAL ASSISTANCE (KHO:2026:77)
item.description:
Children lived alternate weeks with both parents, and Kela paid them social assistance on one parent's application. According to the Supreme Administrative Court the other parent, who could afford to support the children, must repay the assistance. The maintenance obligation does not depend on where the child lives. — The appeal was dismissed. The outcome of the Administrative Court's decision was not changed.

source

item.title: PROPORTIONALITY OF TAX PENALTY (P16-2026-001)
item.description:
The Supreme Court of Ukraine asked the European Court of Human Rights whether a court may reduce a tax penalty fixed by law. According to the Court, courts do not need to have such a power. However, the law as a whole must prevent excessively large penalties. The opinion is not binding. — Advisory opinion delivered.

source

item.title: COJ: STEA CRITERIA PROBLEMATIC (OKV/1653/10/2026 ym.)
item.description:
The ministry announced that certain kinds of organisations would no longer receive continued grants. According to the Chancellor of Justice this could look as if some organisations were excluded in advance. All applications must be assessed on the same, pre-announced conditions, and the reasons for decisions must be recorded. — Opinion: attention was drawn to the grant criteria and the procedure.

source

item.title: EXCLUSION OF TENDERER UPHELD (MAO:461/2026)
item.description:
An entrepreneur submitted a tender in the electronic system using another company's credentials, so the buyer treated that company as the tenderer. The company lacked a required form and did not meet the credit rating requirement, so the tender was excluded. According to the Market Court this was allowed, because a tenderer is responsible for its tender's details. The appeal was dismissed. — The appeal was dismissed.

source

item.title: CITIZENSHIP COMPLAINTS NOT EXAMINED (EOA tiedote 29.9.2026)
item.description:
The Ombudsman will for now not examine complaints about long processing times for citizenship applications at the Immigration Service. The reason is that the Deputy Chancellor of Justice is already monitoring the same issue until June 2027 and will issue a decision on it later.

source

item.title: FCCA: FINNISH MARKETS CONCENTRATED (KKV tiedote 29.9.2026)
item.description:
According to a report by the Finnish Competition and Consumer Authority, many sectors in Finland have few competitors, and new firms enter the market less often than before. This may slow productivity growth. The authority wants more power to intervene in mergers and to impose fines itself.

source

item.title: EXPERT COSTS PAID BY THE STATE (KKO:2026:72)
item.description:
The accused relied on two expert opinions in a rape case. He had a court-appointed defence counsel. According to the Supreme Court both opinions were necessary to clarify the case, so the State pays their costs, 4 430 euros in total. The ruling was decided by a vote. — The State pays the costs of the opinions, 4 430 euros in total (vote).

source

item.title: TIERA WAS NOT AN IN-HOUSE ENTITY (KHO:2026:76)
item.description:
Lohja bought an information system without tendering from a company in which it held a small stake. Buying without tendering is allowed from a company the buyer controls together with the other owners. According to the Supreme Administrative Court, Lohja did not control the company because it had no board representative. The procurement should have been tendered. As the contract had already been made, the procurement decision was not annulled. — The Market Court's decision was overturned. The procurement should have been tendered.

source

item.title: AVERAGE HOURLY PAY MISCALCULATED (TT 2026:33)
item.description:
An employer calculated an employee's average hourly earnings incorrectly. It used a model agreed at the company, although under the collective agreement the calculation must be based on hours worked, and this cannot be agreed otherwise. The employer pays the missing wages except for instalments over five years old. It also pays the union a 4 000 euro compensatory fine for knowingly breaching the agreement. — The action was largely upheld. Compensatory fine 4 000 euros.

source

item.title: FIN-FSA: SIMPLIFYING REGULATION (Finanssivalvonta tiedote 28.9.2026)
item.description:
The FIN-FSA considers that rules for banks and other financial firms can be lightened, as long as firms remain solvent and the financial system stable. The effects of changes must be assessed carefully. Mortgage rules have already been eased this year.

source

item.title: WITHDRAWN CHARGE: RIGHT TO APPEAL (KKO:2026:71)
item.description:
The prosecutor announced that he was dropping the charge because he intended to transfer the case to another EU country. The accused objected. The District Court ended the proceedings and stated that the decision could not be appealed. According to the Supreme Court the accused nevertheless had the right to appeal.

source

item.title: MUNICIPAL AI USE UNDER REVIEW (EOA tiedote 28.9.2026)
item.description:
The Deputy Ombudsman is investigating on her own initiative how AI is used in a municipality's administration. The reason is a reported case in which AI replaced the duties of two managers. The review looks, for example, at whether decision-making remains lawful and how the authority's responsibility is ensured.

source

item.title: AMBEA–HUMANA DEAL APPROVED (KKV/985/14.00.10/2026)
item.description:
The Finnish Competition and Consumer Authority approved without conditions a merger in which Ambea gains control of Humana. Both companies provide, among other things, institutional child welfare care and housing services for people with disabilities.

source

item.title: TAXATION OF LP-FORM FUNDS (VM084:00/2025)
item.description:
The ministry is asking for views on a proposal to change the taxation of private equity funds operating as limited partnerships. The fund's income would be taxed directly in the hands of investors, as if they had invested themselves. The change would mainly concern funds set up from the beginning of 2028.

source

item.title: CHILD'S REPRESENTATIVE AT THE ECHR (ECHR 235 (2026))
item.description:
The Human Rights Court is changing its rules of procedure. It will be able to ask a State to arrange an independent representative for a child to handle the child's case before the Court. The change takes effect in March 2027. — Rules 36 and 44 of the Rules of Court were amended.

source

item.title: UKRAINE CLAIMS COMMISSION TREATY (HE 189/2026 vp)
item.description:
Finland is joining a treaty that sets up an international body to handle compensation claims for damage caused by Russia's war of aggression. Parliament must approve the treaty. A second bill was submitted at the same time on the administration and funding of the special tribunal for the crime of aggression.

source

item.title: CHILD'S PEACE AS AGGRAVATING FACTOR (OM070:00/2024)
item.description:
The ministry is asking for views on a proposal under which violence could be punished more severely if committed in a family or other close relationship within a child's sight or hearing. A child's peace means the child's right to grow up safe without experiencing or witnessing violence.

source

item.title: DETENTION: 6-MONTH LIMIT REACHED (KKO:2026:70)
item.description:
A foreign national may as a rule be detained for at most six months. According to the Supreme Court earlier detention periods also count, even if there are breaks between them. In this case the six-month limit had been reached.

source

item.title: ENERGY PRICE-CHANGE TERMS, CJEU (C-900/24)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The CJEU ruled on when a price-change term in an energy contract may be unfair to the consumer. The exact content must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: DOORSTEP SALES WITHDRAWAL, CJEU (C-381/25)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The judgment concerns a consumer's right to withdraw from a purchase made away from the seller's premises, for example at home. The exact content must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: NOTIFYING EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS (C-369/25)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The judgment concerns an employer's obligation to inform the employee of the essential terms of employment. The exact content must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: WIND FARM PERMIT AND PARTICIPATION (C-151/25)
item.category: Court of Justice of the EU
item.description:
The judgment concerns whether the public must be able to participate when the validity of a wind farm's permit is extended. The exact content must be read from the judgment.

source

item.title: DEGIORGIO V. MALTA: INADMISSIBLE (Degiorgio v. Malta, 26602/25 ja 26731/25)
item.description:
The brothers charged with murdering a Maltese journalist complained that they had too little time to find their own lawyer. They had themselves pleaded guilty. According to the European Court of Human Rights, appointing lawyers for them was reasonable. The application was not admitted, and the decision is final. — Declared inadmissible, unanimously.

source

item.title: COMPOST INSPECTIONS AND PRIVACY (EOAK 2921/2025)
item.description:
The Ombudsman examined whether authorities may inspect people's composters and how privacy must then be protected. She made a proposal on the matter.

source

item.title: GIFT TAX RELIEF, NORTHERN FINLAND (Pohjois-Suomen HaO 1524/2026)
item.description:
A person who receives a business as a gift may have to pay the relieved gift tax if they give up the business too soon. The ruling concerns whether financial difficulties can be a compelling reason to avoid this. Only keywords are available.

source

item.title: GRANT DECISIONS NEEDED REASONS (OKV/678/10/2026 ym.)
item.description:
The minister awarded money to youth organisations but did not explain sufficiently why they met the legal conditions. According to the Chancellor of Justice the decisions needed better reasons, especially because they departed from earlier practice.

source

item.title: MINISTER'S AIDE FINED FOR FRAUD (KKO:2026:69)
item.description:
A minister's special adviser ordered presentation coaching for the minister and had the ministry pay for it. According to the Supreme Court the coaching related to party work, not the minister's work. The adviser was sentenced to 80 day-fines for fraud and breach of official duty.

source

item.title: SHIFT DATA IS NOT SECRET (EOAK 7769/2025)
item.description:
A client asked the wellbeing services county which carers had visited his home. The request was handled too slowly and in the wrong way. According to the Ombudsman, carers' work shifts are not secret information.

source

item.title: WASTE DEAL TO PHASE II REVIEW (KKV/743/14.00.10/2026)
item.description:
The competition authority is examining more closely whether L&T may buy a waste company in North Ostrobothnia. The deal could weaken competition in the region's waste management. The investigation may take months, and the case is pending.

source

item.title: PRISONER WAS WRONGLY RESTRAINED (EOAK 5562/2025)
item.description:
A prisoner was handcuffed many times, for example during outdoor exercise. According to the Ombudsman the prison did not show that the restraint was necessary. The prison therefore acted wrongly.

source

item.title: KUIJT V. NETHERLANDS: INADMISSIBLE (Kuijt v. Alankomaat, 19365/19)
item.description:
The applicant objected to judges who do not vote taking part in the deliberations of the Dutch supreme court. The European Court of Human Rights did not take up the case, because the applicant had not first used all the remedies available in his own country. — Declared inadmissible: domestic remedies not exhausted.

source

item.title: TIME-BARRED DEBT AS ADVANCEMENT (KKO:2026:68)
item.description:
A child owed money to a parent, but the debt became time-barred while the parent was alive. When the parent died, the amount of the time-barred debt was deemed an advancement on the child's inheritance, unless otherwise prescribed. An advancement is taken into account when the estate is divided. — The outcome of the Court of Appeal's judgment is not changed.

source

item.title: CRIMEA'S CHILDREN: ECHR HEARING (Ukrainian Helsinki HR Union v. Venäjä)
item.description:
An organisation has applied on behalf of ten Ukrainian children. The children disappeared from children's homes in Crimea when Russia took control of the area and were allegedly given up for adoption. The Court heard the case in September. The decision will come later.

source

item.title: COLOMBIA WITHDRAWS FROM CASE, ICJ (Etelä-Afrikka v. Israel)
item.description:
Colombia had joined the case between South Africa and Israel concerning the Genocide Convention and Gaza. Colombia has now withdrawn from it. The case itself continues at the International Court of Justice.

source

item.title: SCHOOL GOOGLE PLATFORM: NEW RULING (TSV/40/2018)
item.description:
A school may use Google's education platform with pupils' data only to the extent that teaching requires. Google or others may not use pupils' data for their own purposes, such as developing services. The decision may be appealed.

source

item.title: HUNTING ACT: NGO APPEAL RIGHTS (MMM, lausuntopyyntö)
item.description:
The ministry proposes that a nature or environmental organisation could appeal against hunting decisions only if it operates in the area on an established basis and has been registered for at least three years. Comments may be submitted by 20.10.2026. This is only a proposal.

source

item.title: HEADSCARF AND POLICE FORCE, KKO (KKO:2026:67)
item.description:
Asylum seekers refused on religious grounds to remove their headscarves for a police photograph. The Supreme Court assessed whether the police were allowed to use force to take the photo. The outcome of the Court of Appeal's judgment stands. The ruling was decided by a vote. — The outcome of the Court of Appeal's judgment is not changed.

source

item.title: EXCISE DUTY: NO ESTIMATED TAXATION (KHO:2026:75)
item.description:
The tax authority assessed excise duty on the basis of precise Customs data, even though no tax return had been filed. According to the Supreme Administrative Court this was not estimated taxation, so the tax increase could not be the 25 per cent applicable to estimated taxation.

source

item.title: ROAD ASSOCIATION'S FEE WAS VALID (KKO:2026:66)
item.description:
A road shareholder temporarily used a private road in a way that differed greatly from normal use. The road association imposed a usage fee on him. According to the Supreme Court the fee did not have to match the extra costs caused to the road. The fee was lawful.

source

item.title: DISMISSED EMPLOYEE GETS NO DAMAGES (KKO:2026:65)
item.description:
A regional manager accepted equipment in machinery deals that did not belong to the customer and recorded its data incorrectly. The money-laundering charges were dismissed, but according to the Supreme Court the employer did not have to pay him compensation for the dismissal.

source

item.title: ALIENS ACT: DETENTION (Sisäministeriö)
item.description:
The Government is preparing changes to when a foreign national may be detained and how a refusal of entry at the border can be appealed. Anyone may submit comments by 16.10.2026.

source

item.title: LEASING + DEVICE COVER: ONE SUPPLY (KHO:2026:74)
item.description:
A leasing company sold device cover alongside the leased equipment. According to the Supreme Administrative Court the device cover was not insurance but part of the same leasing service. For VAT purposes the whole is one supply, and the company may deduct the VAT on repair costs.

source

item.title: PAY GRADE BY SKILL LEVEL (TT 2026:32)
item.description:
In the construction sector the pay grade is determined by what the employee can do, not by the job title. A skilled worker belongs at least to pay grade IV.

source

item.title: COUNCIL MAY REMOVE COMMITTEE CHAIRS (KHO:2026:73)
item.description:
A municipal council may, because of a loss of confidence, remove a committee's chair and vice-chair in the middle of their term. According to the Supreme Administrative Court they may at the same time be removed from committee membership, and the whole committee need not be removed. The ruling was decided by a vote.

source

item.title: SWEDISH WEB CONTENT, OMBUDSMAN (EOAK 3844/2025)
item.description:
The decision concerns whether Statistics Finland's website has enough information in Swedish. Read the outcome in the decision.

source

item.title: RENTAL APPLICATIONS KEPT 12 YEARS (TSV/1319/2025)
item.description:
A rental housing agency kept applicants' data for 12 years. According to the data protection authority that is too long. The data must usually be deleted after five years. The company received a reprimand and must change its practice.

source

item.title: INHERITANCE TAX: FULL RELIEF (KHO:2026:72)
item.description:
An heir inherited shares in a limited company and was entitled to generational transfer relief. According to the Supreme Administrative Court the relief covered all the shares, even though most of the company's assets related to real estate and rental activity. The heir also received 1 500 euros for the delay in the proceedings. — The case was returned to the Tax Administration to grant the relief for the shares in full. A was awarded 1 500 euros in compensation for the delay in the proceedings.

source

item.title: LATE-BILLED CLIENT FEES (KHO:2026:71)
item.description:
The City of Helsinki invoiced client fees late through its own fault, and a family received one large bill. According to the Supreme Administrative Court, when considering a reduction of the fees, all fees that fell due at the same time should have been looked at together. The case was returned to the city. — The decisions were overturned and the case returned to the City of Helsinki for reconsideration.

source

item.title: NICARAGUA V. GERMANY: HEARINGS OVER (Nicaragua v. Saksa)
item.description:
Nicaragua accuses Germany of neglecting its obligations in the Palestinian territories, among other things through arms exports. Germany says the Court cannot decide the case. The Court heard both sides and will first decide whether it can hear the case.

source

item.title: TERVEYSTALO–HOHDE CLEARED ON TERMS (KKV – yrityskauppavalvonta)
item.description:
Terveystalo was allowed to buy the Hohde dental chain on condition that it sells its dental operations in Savonlinna, Mikkeli and Seinäjoki. This preserves competition. For the first time, the FCCA gave conditional clearance already at the initial stage of the review.

source

item.title: VANUATU SUES FRANCE OVER ISLANDS (Vanuatu v. Ranska)
item.description:
Vanuatu wants the International Court of Justice to confirm that two small islands belong to it and not to France. The maritime boundary would be settled at the same time. The case can proceed only if France agrees.

source

item.title: PRIVATE ROAD GRANT: APPEAL FAILS (Itä-Suomen HaO 2167/2026)
item.description:
The authority left about 46 000 euros of private road improvement costs outside the state grant. The Administrative Court dismissed the appeal, so the decision stands.

source

item.title: SECURITY CLEARANCE AND DISMISSAL (Pohjois-Suomen HaO 1285/2026)
item.description:
The Tax Administration dismissed an employee because he refused a security clearance, citing a reduction in work. According to the Administrative Court there was no less work; the reason related to the employee's own conduct. That ground for dismissal could therefore not be used, and the decision was overturned.

source

item.title: SOCIAL WORK DEMAND LEVEL, LABOUR CT (TT 2026:31)
item.description:
A joint municipal authority reassessed social workers' duties as less demanding. According to the Labour Court it breached the agreement, and the duties belong to demand level 2.

source

item.title: ENDED DOPING BAN NOT PUBLIC (TSV/179/2021)
item.description:
The sports integrity centre published information on an athlete's minor doping violation even though the ban had already ended. There was no basis for publishing it. SUEK received a reprimand and an order to correct its practices.

source

item.title: RÄSÄNEN APPLICATION PENDING AT ECHR (Räsänen v. Suomi (vireillä))
item.description:
Päivi Räsänen was fined by the Supreme Court for ethnic agitation. She has applied to the European Court of Human Rights, relying on freedom of expression and religion. The judgment nevertheless stands. The proceedings may take years.

source

item.title: SMUGGLING CASE: RUSSIA AND POLAND (Liettua v. Valko-Venäjä)
item.description:
Lithuania accuses Belarus of helping migrants cross the border illegally. Poland and Russia want to present their views on the interpretation of the treaty, and the EU also gave its views. The case is pending.

source

item.title: TEMPORARY BUILDING, DEVIATION (Helsingin HaO 4926/2026)
item.description:
The case concerns a temporary building: whether a separate deviation permit is needed, or whether a building permit suffices when the deviation is minor. Only keywords are available.

source

item.title: DR CONGO FILES CASE AGAINST RWANDA (Kongon DT v. Ruanda)
item.description:
Congo accuses Rwanda of serious acts of violence in eastern Congo over decades. Congo has taken the matter to the International Court of Justice. The proceedings have only just begun.

source

item.title: COMPENSATORY FINE FOR WAGES, TT (TT 2026:30)
item.description:
The case concerns the payment of wages and whether the employer breached the collective agreement in a way that leads to a compensatory fine. Read the outcome in the ruling.

source
